title: A Novel PCR Method for Detecting ACE Gene Insertion/Deletion Polymorphisms
author: Yang, Liang, et al.

steps.title: Collect blood in EDTA tubes
steps.instruction: Draw fresh whole blood into tubes containing ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) and keep the samples on the bench.

steps.title: Prepare NaOH mixture
steps.instruction: Mix the blood with 100 mM NaOH at a 1:2 (blood:NaOH) volume ratio to obtain a total volume of 30 µL, then incubate the mixture at room temperature for 2 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Calculate volumes so that blood + NaOH = 30 µL (e.g., 10 µL blood + 20 µL 100 mM NaOH).
Leave the tube on the bench (≈20‑25 °C) for exactly 2 minutes.

steps.title: Add template to PCR
steps.instruction: Pipette 5 µL of the NaOH‑treated mixture directly into the PCR reaction; the template must be used immediately and cannot be stored or reused.

steps.title: Store remaining blood samples
steps.instruction: Keep unused whole‑blood aliquots at 4 °C for up to 1 week or freeze at –20 °C; do not subject any sample to more than three freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Perform Direct PCR‑LFA genotyping
steps.instruction: Run the ACE insertion/deletion PCR using the Direct PCR‑LFA system according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Extract DNA for gel validation
steps.instruction: Use the whole‑blood genomic DNA isolation kit (Xi’an GoldMag Nanobiotech Co., Ltd.) to purify DNA from blood samples that will be analysed by agarose‑gel electrophoresis.

steps.title: Run 2% agarose gel electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Separate the PCR products on a 2 % agarose gel and visualise bands to confirm ACE genotypes.

steps.title: Sequence a subset of samples
steps.instruction: Randomly select 100 case samples and submit their PCR products for DNA sequencing.

steps.title: Statistical comparison of methods
steps.instruction: Compare the genotyping results obtained from the Direct PCR‑LFA system with those from 2 % agarose‑gel electrophoresis (and sequencing) using appropriate statistical analyses.
